gold: Drug-induced blepharitis and ectropion associated with TNF-α inhibitors (infliximab and adalimumab)
e7_s4_rationale: The patient's ocular symptoms started while on infliximab therapy and switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse, suggesting a possible association between the TNF-α inhibitor treatment and the ocular manifestations.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
e7_s4_rejected.why: While Crohn disease can cause ocular inflammation, the specific timing of the symptoms in relation to the TNF-α inhibitor treatment suggests a more direct link to the medication rather than the disease itself.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
e7_s4_rejected.why: The patient was switched to adalimumab after the ocular symptoms appeared, making it less likely to be the primary cause.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Blepharitis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Although the patient has symptoms consistent with blepharitis, such as crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, the context of TNF-α inhibitor use and the broader range of ocular findings suggest a more complex condition.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
e7_s4_rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms or other findings typical of Sjögren's syndrome, such as dry mouth or positive autoantibodies, making this diagnosis less likely.
